It feels like the bride and the groom are aligned and on the same page instead of one wanting to extract from the other as fast as possible

Pretty bullish

This is what I wish someone told me when I was going through shit

Your perspective is skewed by what glasses you are wearing i.e your thoughts and your mental state, which can all change either through physical / direct injections (drugs), or mental control 

with a change in mental state nothing is impossible, i've seen poor people be extremely happy. and what mental states are, are essentially thoughts + emotion = belief; and so rewiring the belief is as simple as looking at the opposite - e.g i have the belief that i'm not good enough -> what if i am good enough ; and then taking action to truly show that 

scientifically many studies and religions point to all the same outcomes for mental health and it is very much a solved game - that's the good thing about living in the 21st century. changing your mental state is important, but also, the other thing that works is that your mind really really hates boredom

so when you are in flow state, you are essentially in a one-pointed mind state - your mind is focusing on one thing, and one thing only. depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, paranoia, all have their roots in the opposite of this - too much thought. the alleviation here is to go out and run. sports. anything that activates your parasymphatetic nervous system. in particular, don't work out - instead, you want to do activities like running, gymnastics, and preferably, social - dance, hiit classes, boxing, muay thai, and really - sports is great for this

and once you do that you find that your thoughts and your mind calms down a lot in the day. the essence of this entire answer lies in treating mental health like a problem with a cause and effect

Too much thought -> cause is too little action ; take action 

Interaction with thought / feeling bad -> have to change your Default Network Mode to face your emotions, and reorganize your beliefs

Essentially modern living is genuinely bad for *being human* and it is important to spend time in nature and do things that are *human* like running and sports. And then once you are in a better state of mind, you can tackle whatever emotion you are running away from - because frankly, its never about the thing itself. It's always about what the thing makes you feel. When I lost a bunch of money, it was never the money. It was the association that money was safety, and by losing money, I had somehow lost the safety I had. And then I was also angry, and had a bunch of self-regret, and all around I had a lot of negative emotions that I was running away from and didn't confront. 

The weird and simple solution is - feel your feelings, and they get better. You are not a rock, and much of modern life focuses on humans trying to be like robots - either working slave like hours, or just generally showing emotion seems to be seen as a form of weakness in this era especially in the corporate world 

But feelings are just feelings, and when you feel them, they just go away. It's why you feel better after crying - feelings don't stay there forever when you process them. The only reason they stay there, is because humans rather avoid them instead.

Anyways, I typed this because again - I think while a lot of advice is well-meaning, this is what I wish I had when I was going through shit - practical, real advice from someone who actually knew his shit. Things like time heals, this too shall pass - they're all well and good, but they don't really tell you how to work through it. 

Hope this helps. Lots of love, 

Kyle
